cards.title: Polymer and Coacervate Nanostructures
cards.description: Liquid-liquid phase separation of block copolymers produces coacervates: membraneless, concentrated droplets that act as precursors to solid-phase materials. Imaging their internal structure shows how these intermediates govern the self-assembly that follows.

slides.description: Amphiphilic block copolymers vesicles spreading as they undergo bilayer formation. Automated segmentation algorithm tracks and quantifies growth.

slides.title: Increased selectivity for photosynthetic Z-Scheme H2 evolution over reduction of the ferric ion redox mediator enabled by atomic layer deposition of ultrathin oxide coatings on Rh-doped SrTiO3 nanoparticles decorated with Pt cocatalysts
slides.description: STEM-EDS of SrTiO3 nanoreactors (cyan) revealing FeOx deposits (yellow) which form during water-to-hydrogen-gas conversion and inhibit the reaction.

slides.title: Direct Observation of Rh and La Dopant Positions in SrTiO3 Nanoparticles with Atomic-Scale Electron Microscopy
slides.description: STEM-EDS analysis pipeline for Rh-doped SrTiO3. ~100 double-unit cells were averaged to reveal Rh dopants occupy both the A-site and B-site, with the majority sitting in the B-site.

slides.title: Toward Imaging Defect-Mediated Energy Transfer between Single Nanocrystal Donors and Single Molecule Acceptors
slides.description: TEM images of ZnO Nanocrystals with internal defect voids highlighted by the red arrows. Note the high level of defocus was intentional to better capture the voids.

cards.title: Florescence Microscopy
cards.description: Optical microscopy reaches the length and time scales electron imaging cannot: millimetre fields, minute-long processes, samples left unperturbed. It supplies the bulk context that high-resolution measurements are interpreted against.

cards.title: Nanoscale Electrochemistry
cards.description: Applying a potential inside the microscope drives assembly and disassembly on demand. Electrochemical input becomes a controlled experimental variable, so structural response can be measured against a known driving force rather than inferred afterwards.

slides.title: Observing the Dynamics of an Electrochemically Driven Active Material with Liquid Electron Microscopy
slides.description: Custom DSSIM analysis algorithm visualizes and quantifies polymer self assembly occurring near a microelectrode. (Left) Processed data. (Right) DSSIM algorithm highlighting structural change

cards.title: Cryo Electron Microscopy
cards.description: Vitrification holds transient structures still long enough for high-resolution two- and three-dimensional imaging. Pairing cryo snapshots with in situ kinetics gives both what a structure is and how it came to be.

slides.title: CryoEM reveals the complex self-assembly of a chemically driven disulfide hydrogel
slides.description: Template matching identifies stack-fiber phase in CryoEM image dataset. Animation shows that when the template aligns with the stacked fibers, they are identified in the image.
